checked: Readers table covers every Bun assumption named in the intent, plus the two recognisers added in review outcomes
No-profile fallback is stated exactly (built-in derived filter, Architect commands, Fallow as now)
Unproven-command handling: stored with recorded result, never run unattended
Owner confirmation of commands is defined for init and for later changes
Build order dependencies against the runtime split are stated
src/runner/quality-failure.ts:16-19 confirms the Bun-only recogniser the plan says to replace

target.unit: Review outcomes: Each build step states its acceptance check

findings.what: No build step has an acceptance check or verification command; the plan says each step states one and names only a first check (a profile for this repo, an npm fixture and a cargo fixture, each proven by running its commands).
findings.failureScenario: A builder ships steps 2-5 with unit tests that mock the profile. The recognisers, auto-fix, isolated recheck and Fallow still behave as Bun-only when run against the npm or cargo fixture, and nothing fails. 'Proven by running its commands' also passes with a stub that records exit 0 without executing anything.
evidence: "Each build step states its acceptance check; the first is a profile for this repository, for an npm fixture and for a cargo fixture"
findings.suggestion: Per step, give an observable check on the npm and cargo fixtures: step 2 refused/misclassified commands now accepted and a failing cargo test classified as a test failure; step 4 isolated cargo recheck gets its dependencies and runs; step 5 audit off or on per profile, map built from source.

findings.what: The plan migrates repo_map_sources into the profile and removes it, but also says no profile means today's behaviour and validation rejects empty verify. A project with an existing source row and no verify commands has no valid profile to migrate into.
findings.failureScenario: Builder either creates profiles with empty verify (violating validation, and ending the 'no profile' fallback), or drops existing custom source filters, silently changing repository maps for those projects.
evidence: "It is migrated into the profile (keyed by project key) and removed"
findings.suggestion: State what migration produces for rows without a profile: keep rows until init writes a profile, or allow a source-only profile.

target.unit: Fields made precise in the build

findings.what: Behaviour-changing fields are deferred to the build: how changed paths reach a fix command, ordering and scope across two toolchains, and whether a failing verify command stops later ones.
findings.failureScenario: Builder picks one: fix runs on the whole tree instead of changed files, or mixed-toolchain verify runs in an arbitrary order. Different observable edits to worker commits and different failure classification.
evidence: "how changed paths are passed to a `fix` command; ordering and scope of commands across two toolchains"
findings.suggestion: Decide: files substituted as appended arguments vs placeholder; verify runs in array order, all commands run even after a failure or stop at first.

findings.what: Dismissal of the setup notice has no stated scope or storage (per project, per user, resettable), and it is unstated whether init prompts again after a failed or abandoned setup session.
findings.failureScenario: Dismiss is held in GUI memory and the notice returns on every window open, or dismiss is global and hides setup for all projects.
evidence: "The notice stays until the owner sets up or dismisses it."
findings.suggestion: State: per project key, stored with the profile store, cleared by 'Run setup again'.

findings.what: Confirmation state is not defined: where the confirmed flag lives, what happens to unconfirmed edits (stored as a pending revision or not at all), and whether the runtime runs the last confirmed revision while a change is pending.
findings.failureScenario: Builder stores the Architect's proposal directly as active with a confirmed boolean never checked by the runtime, so unattended commands run unreviewed.
evidence: "a later change to a command, including a re-run of setup, shows the difference and needs the owner's confirm"
findings.suggestion: Say: revisions are append-only; only the latest confirmed revision is read by the runtime; a proposal is a pending revision.

questions.question: For a project that has a stored repo_map_sources row but no profile, what should the migration produce?
questions.why: Decides whether the map filter survives and whether a source-only profile is a valid state.
options: Keep the row until init writes a profile, then drop it
Create a source-only profile with empty verify allowed
Drop the row; the built-in derived filter applies

questions.question: When a profile has two toolchains, do verify commands run in array order and stop at the first failure?
questions.why: Changes failure classification and cost per check run.
options: Array order, stop at first failure
Array order, run all and report every failure
Grouped by toolchain, run in parallel
